source_name: IBM Developer tutorials (developer.ibm.com) - the watsonx Orchestrate / IBM Bob surface, incl. the BPMN-to-agent tutorial
enumeration_method: the site's own sitemap, declared in robots.txt as Sitemap: https://developer.ibm.com/middleware/v1/sitemap.xml. It enumerates 1982 URLs (tutorials 713, articles 578, learningpaths 419, blogs 95, components 80, technologies 32, series 25, devpractices 13, depmodels 8, languages 7, terms 6, and one each of /, /about/, /badges/, /exchanges/, /ibm-fintech/, /product-doclinks/, plus 13 type index pages). All 1982 were fetched: 1606 through the site's own JSON content endpoint /middleware/v1/contents/<type>/<slug>, 376 (the Learning-Path item pages and the index pages) by direct HTML fetch with the body taken from the Next.js flight payload, and any URL the JSON endpoint 404s by direct HTML fetch as well. No keyword filter and no facet was used: the sitemap is the site's complete enumeration. Two GitHub surfaces linked from the source were enumerated separately through the GitHub tree API (IBM/oic-i-agentic-ai-tutorials, 1405 entries, truncated=false; IBM/ibm-watsonx-orchestrate-adk, 1994 entries) - together exactly one .bpmn file exists in them, recorded as its own item.
browser_tool: chrome-devtools-mcp (cdp1), own tab; pages also fetched with curl at ~0.3 req/s
note: Census unit: PAGE for all 1982 sitemap rows, plus the one repository .bpmn file = population 1983. Rows n=1..1982 follow the sitemap order, so n equals the line number in the frontier file; n=1983 is the repository item, appended last because it cannot be reached from the sitemap. 108 Learning-Path item pages reproduce an in-population tutorial wholesale (all of their images come from that one tutorial's image folder) and are recorded as E3-duplicate of it; the mapping is in ledgers/ibm-developer-watsonx.raw/html/lp_embed_map.tsv. HOW EXCLUSIONS WERE DRAWN. Every page that carried a candidate signal (an AI/BPMN keyword in its body, or a model-shaped image) was reviewed: its figures were rendered into contact sheets and looked at, or, where the page has no figure at all (72 pages, html/visual.d/20_nofig.json) the page body was ruled on textually. Pages with no candidate signal get the mechanical E0 with a verbatim quote from the page body, which is what makes keyword absence auditable. The source has no BPMN XML and exactly one live bpmn-js canvas, and each row carries judged_from naming what was opened. Two codes cover almost all exclusions: E0-no-artefact where the figure is not a drawn process at all (a UI screenshot, a table, a chart, a code listing, a network graphic), or where the drawing's connected items are systems/components/data/tiers (architecture, deployment, data-flow, taxonomy) with no ordered activity sequence; E1-not-bpmn where ordered activities or steps ARE joined by directed connectors but in a recognisable non-BPMN convention, which the row names in words (Mermaid render, LangGraph graph, ISO-5807 flowchart, vendor flow canvases, CRISP-DM phase cycle, chevron stage bar). Where a page-asserted process or life-cycle artefact is drawn with no connectors at all, or where participant boxes are joined by numbered/labelled interaction flows that read as steps, the row is UNCERTAIN with a tailored question rather than an exclusion - those are the corpus's borderline cases and they are surfaced deliberately. judgment=true marks the rows where a notation call was actually made (E1 rows and all INCLUDE/UNCERTAIN rows); judgment=false marks the mechanical E0 rows, and also the Learning-Path pages that inherit a reason from the tutorial they reproduce - their notation call is that tutorial's own row, not a second one made here, so ten of them carry an inherited E1 reason under judgment=false. No row uses E2-no-ai-element: the source is AI-saturated, so an E0/E1 exclusion here rests on the figure not being a process artefact or not being BPMN, never on the absence of an AI element. RECODE AND SELF-AUDIT (2026-09-26). The first pass sent every page whose figure is a drawn architecture / component / block / pipeline / agent diagram through the mechanical E0-no-artefact with judgment=false, which hid 190 notation calls behind a code that claims no judgement was made. CLAUDE.md sec 3 names an architecture box diagram as an E1 example and prompts/02b states the convention (a drawn non-BPMN diagram is judgment:true; a screenshot of a UI, table, form or code listing is judgment:false), so those rows were recoded to E1-not-bpmn with judgment:true as superseding rows (html/supersedes.json; the first-pass coding came from decide.py's arch class, which has been left in place - this ledger supersedes it rather than rewriting the tool). The self-audit that prompts/02_source-census.md step 3 asks for then re-opened the recoded figures and put prompts/02b's question to each: could this be an ordered process with an AI step that a researcher might read as BPMN-like? Every figure carrying process semantics - start/end nodes, a split that merges, numbered or ordered activity-labelled steps, or an activity-labelled connector - was flipped to UNCERTAIN with a record and a tailored question (html/flips.json, corpus records 034-047); figures whose connected items are systems, components, tiers, zones, trees, cards, charts, wireframes or unlabelled nodes stayed E1-not-bpmn. One candidate recode was put back by that audit: n=1250's figure, which the page's alt text calls a node-capacity diagram, is a capture of a resource-pool form in a running console, so it stays E0-no-artefact with judgment=false. The share this produces is 12.9% rather than 4.0%, and that is reported rather than forced down: it is the same exclusion decisions, now labelled as the notation calls they always were. It is above the 10% ceiling in tools/audit.py (reported to the orchestrator, 2026-09-26, not edited around). The only ways under the ceiling would be to code a drawn architecture diagram as "no artefact" - the fault this correction fixes - or to claim hesitation I do not have about a layer diagram, which would dilute the very signal the ceiling exists to protect. The ceiling is a triage heuristic and the 256 rows it flags are the ones to sample: every one of them names the notation it is drawn in, and the 46 UNCERTAIN rows are the ones where I could not. What the self-audit re-opened, precisely: all 143 rows whose reviewed note mentions a flow, step, stage, order or sequence (the 133 in html/selfaudit.tsv plus ten further suspects found by a wider keyword net; montages figs/SA1-SA14, which is where the 14 flips were decided), plus 3 figures that had to be re-fetched and re-rendered before they could be judged at all (n=316, n=215, n=245); the remaining rows were re-checked from their reviewed notes, each of which describes layers, panels, tiers, zones, trees, charts, tables, wireframes or neural-network schematics and names no ordered activity sequence.
